newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Climatologist sees good SAfrica maize, sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: Climatologist sees good SAfrica maize, sugar crop.

text.p: Weather patterns suggest South Africa will enjoy another good agricultural year in 1997, the Climate and Weather Research Laboratory at the University of Cape Town said on Tuesday in its latest outlook.

The Free State province was seen producing a maize yield 51 percent above normal, although South Africa as a whole was seen producing a near-normal crop which would be down on last year's bumper 9.5 million tonne harvest. Output in 1995 was 4.41 million.
The KwaZulu Natal-Swaziland sugar industry was seen raising cane production 39 percent above normal with cane yield 52 percent above normal.
South Africa sugar production totalled 2.37 million tonnes this year, up sharply on the 1995 total of 1.67 million.
Neighbouring Zimbabwe, however, with early summer rainfall likely to drop 16 percent below normal, was seen producing a national maize yield total of 31 percent below normal.
Overall, the picture is of reasonable rainfall in most of southern Africa.
"Climatic signals during November in respect of 1996/97 summer rainfall over southern Africa continued to support adequate rains," director Mark Jury said in the outlook.

But he added that climatic trends suggested an early end to the season was expected, particularly in the Limpopo area. However, cool sea temperatures in the tropical southeast Atlantic may enhance late summer rains over southeast Namibia.

Forecasting early summer (November to early January) rain, Jury said the Eastern Cape would have rainfall of 40 percent above normal, the Northwest Free State 23 percent below normal, Gauteng-North Mpumalanga Highveld 31 percent below normal and Swaziland-Kwazulu Natal-Lowveld would have 25 percent below.

In late summer (mid-January to March) most of South Africa would have near normal rainfall with the Eastern Cape enjoying rainfall 14 percent higher than normal, the Northwest Free State 13 percent below, Gauteng-North Mpumalanga Highveld eight percent above and Swaziland-Kwazulu Natal-Lowveld 30 percent above.
For the period December-February Gauteng's maximum temperature was seen 35 percent above normal. --Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
